title: Let Hollis Have It
hook: His bumper is in the left glass. Again.
scene: Overcast afternoon on I-90 east, three lanes. You are in the center, holding a clean number. In the left door glass a lifted truck fills the view — Hollis, too close, no gap you can count. The right lane is empty wet asphalt. Brake-checking him is a story he will finish with your rear doors. The highway move is to give him a lane and let him be someone else's problem.
decision: Hollis is on your tail in the center. The right is empty. What do you do?

options.text: Signal right, take the empty lane, let him have the center
options.result: One change. He blows past in the center. Your following distance is yours again. You did not write a brake lamp into his windshield.

options.text: Tap the brakes to tell him he is too close
options.result: Your lamps hit his glass. He stands on it or he climbs you. Either way you taught a tailgater with light. The empty lane was the sentence.

options.text: Hold the center and drop ten so the gap in front of you looks safer
options.result: You slow in front of a man who will not. The gap behind dies. You spent your own cushion to keep a lane he wanted.

options.text: Speed up until he cannot match the Ledger
options.result: He matches. Then he matches more. You bought a race on a highway. The empty right was still empty.

debrief: Watch the glass for tailgaters and move to another lane so they can pass. Hollis took the center and left your doors alone.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part two
source.teaching_target: Watch mirrors for tailgaters and move to another lane to let them pass.
